# slug: # Bugs filed in a module board that does NOT own their code, with the SIGNAL each verdict
# rests on: `fixed-in` means a commit SHA said so and is exact; `prose` means the entry named
# a source path in its text and is weaker. Frozen so that a NEW misfiling
# fails while the existing ones do not block anyone — a check that is red on arrival gets
# ignored, and an ignored check is worse than none.
# Routing is by `lane:` (specs/work-tracking-layout.md), and `lane` came from a keyword
# heuristic, which is why these exist. Fixing one means MOVING the entry to the owning
# module's board and deleting its row here; the check reports rows that are no longer
# misfiled, so a stale row cannot sit unnoticed.
# SIX ROWS ADDED 2026-08-17, and they are DEBT RECORDED rather than paid. The gate offers three
# remedies — move the entry, move the code, or baseline it with a reason — and for these six the
# first is not available: `v1/lang/core`, `uniml` and `v1/runtime/backend/rust` have NO board of
# their own (`git ls-files '*BUGS.md'` lists nine, none of them theirs), so there is nowhere to
# move an entry TO. Four of the six name the typer.
# The alternative was leaving `ci.yml`'s validate job red, which it had been since 2026-08-11 on
# exactly this check. This file's own header says why that is worse: a check that is red on
# arrival gets ignored. What is owed is a board for those modules, or an area map that routes
# their entries to an existing one — not another row here.
